title: Conformal quantile convention probes: harnesses for auditing finite-sample validity in conformal-prediction implementations
description:
Measurement harnesses used to audit how Python conformal-prediction implementations resolve the conformal quantile at finite sample sizes.

Each script validates its closed forms against exact rational arithmetic at import time, and each writes a plain-text output file committed alongside it. Two of those self-checks caught errors in their own author's hand-derived assertions, which is the reason they exist.

  • branch_d_check.py — the convention in isolation: an uncorrected level versus the required order statistic on identical draws, 200k draws per cell, fractions.Fraction oracle.
  • convention_probe.py — structural branch identification, coverage sweeps with paired standard errors, threshold extraction.
  • run_sktime_river.py — sktime ConformalIntervals through predict_interval and river RegressionJackknife through predict_one, with an oracle independent of both.
  • run_darts.py — exact rank arithmetic, paired Monte Carlo, and an end-to-end run through a real ConformalNaiveModel.
  • run_statsforecast.py, verify_statsforecast_rebuttal.py — window mapping, and the probe that adjudicated and retracted a finding of the author's own.

Third-party library sources are deliberately not included; probe-requirements.txt pins the versions instead.
